node-1.label: A 27-year-old woman presented with elevated hepatobiliary enzymes

node-2.label: The patient occasionally drank alcohol and was taking axitinib, azelnidipine, and tramadol hydrochloride

node-3.label: The patient had no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease

node-4.label: After stopping alcohol and axitinib, the patient's hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged

node-5.label: Physical examination showed no specific findings

why.why: The liver biopsy showing PAX8-positive malignant cells in Glisson's capsule with destruction of interlobular bile ducts confirms a metastatic malignancy causing perihilar obstruction, providing a definitive structural etiology. This, together with unchanged enzymes after stopping alcohol and axitinib, makes drug-induced liver injury very unlikely.

The liver biopsy reveals malignant infiltration of Glisson's capsule and bile ducts rather than hepatocellular disease, establishing metastatic obstruction. Normal physical findings and absence of viral, autoimmune, metabolic, or steatohepatitis etiologies further argue against chronic liver disease.

The liver biopsy demonstrating PAX8-positive malignant cells with destruction of interlobular bile ducts confirms that the cholestatic enzyme elevation and hilar irregular isoechoic area are due to biliary/cholestatic disease from malignant obstruction. The radiologist explicitly states that immune-mediated cholangiopathy is excluded by the biopsy, so confidence is raised.

node-9.label: Laboratory tests show ALP 1028 U/L and GGT 257 U/L

node-10.label: Ultrasound shows rough uneven liver parenchyma and an irregular isoechoic area from the porta hepatis to the right dorsal side

node-11.label: The patient may have an immune-mediated intrahepatic cholangiopathy such as primary biliary cholangitis

why.why: Liver biopsy shows malignant cells infiltrating and destroying interlobular bile ducts, confirming an obstructive malignant etiology. The radiologist notes that immune-mediated cholangiopathy is excluded by these biopsy findings; although AMA/ANA serology is pending, the malignant infiltration makes primary biliary cholangitis very unlikely.

node-12.label: The patient may have extrahepatic/perihilar biliary obstruction

why.why: The biopsy finding of PAX8-positive malignant cells in Glisson's capsule with destruction of interlobular bile ducts directly confirms extrahepatic/perihilar biliary obstruction. CT/MRI enhancement patterns in the hilar region provide correlative imaging support, so confidence is raised.

node-13.label: Immune-mediated intrahepatic cholangiopathy (e.g., primary biliary cholangitis)

why.why: Biopsy evidence of malignant infiltration destroying interlobular bile ducts excludes immune-mediated intrahepatic cholangiopathy as the cause. The radiologist's interpretation confirms this, so primary biliary cholangitis is no longer a viable leading diagnosis.

Liver biopsy confirms malignant cells in the portal tract destroying interlobular bile ducts, which is direct evidence of extrahepatic/perihilar obstruction. The corresponding CT/MRI enhancement pattern and cholestatic labs support this, and the pathologist's analysis also places metastatic obstruction as the most credible hypothesis.

node-15.label: Perihilar biliary obstruction due to metastatic malignancy (e.g., renal cell carcinoma metastasis)

why.why: Biopsy reveals PAX8-positive malignant cells in Glisson's capsule, a staining pattern consistent with renal cell carcinoma metastasis, and the tumor destroys interlobular bile ducts causing perihilar obstruction. The patient's axitinib use further supports RCC as the primary source. node-16.label: Perihilar biliary obstruction due to perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (Klatskin tumor)

node-17.label: Perihilar biliary obstruction due to benign inflammatory stricture (e.g., primary sclerosing cholangitis or IgG4-related disease)

why.why: Biopsy confirms malignant infiltration of the portal tract rather than an inflammatory process. Therefore a benign inflammatory stricture such as primary sclerosing cholangitis or IgG4-related disease is highly unlikely.

node-18.label: Perihilar biliary obstruction due to choledocholithiasis/Mirizzi syndrome

why.why: The biopsy-proven malignant mass at the porta hepatis provides a definitive structural cause of obstruction, and there is no stone-related evidence. Choledocholithiasis/Mirizzi syndrome is thus very unlikely.
